title: Indian IT Shares Surge as 'Anti-AI' Trade Lifts Nifty IT 2,000 Points in Two Days
excerpt: HCLTech gained nearly 11% in two sessions after its Q2 results, with TCS and Infosys up 6-10%, as a global AI selloff driven by bubble warnings pushed investors toward Indian IT as the 'anti-AI' trade.
body:
• The Nifty IT index soared more than 2,000 points in two sessions to cross 30,000 on Wednesday, its first time above that level in nearly a month.
  • HCLTech rose nearly 11% in two days after reporting 21% year-on-year profit growth to Rs 5,132 crore in Q2 FY27 and raising growth guidance; TCS and Infosys rallied 6-10%.
  • The rally is being driven by an 'anti-AI' trade: as global AI stocks sold off on bubble warnings, investors rotated into Indian IT names previously punished on AI disruption fears.
  • Analysts are split on follow-through — Motilal Oswal sees improving sentiment, while others warn of profit-booking after a sharp two-day move.

Shares of Tata Consultancy Services, HCL Technologies and Infosys extended sharp gains as the global AI frenzy continued to fizzle out, boosting sentiment for India's IT stocks, which are being seen as the so-called 'anti-AI' trade, The Economic Times reported. The Nifty IT index has soared more than 2,000 points over two sessions to cross 30,000 on Wednesday.

Heavyweight HCLTech shares soared nearly 11% in two days since its Q2 results, while TCS and Infosys rallied 6-10% over the same period.

How the 'anti-AI' trade formed

The rally follows a sharp selloff in Indian IT this year, driven by multiple headwinds, with AI the most prominent: as hyperscalers increased spending on the technology, sceptics argued new innovations would displace the sector's workforce-heavy delivery model. That selloff in software stocks was dubbed the 'SaaSpocalypse' by Jefferies' equity trading desk, in Bloomberg's telling.

The turn came as investors began questioning the optimism around AI itself. Michael Burry, known for predicting the 2008 housing crisis, has been warning that the market is in a 'denial' phase over AI spending. The latest leg of the global AI selloff followed Broadcom CEO Hock Tan's remark that many AI investors are behaving like casino gamblers, betting on something they understand very little — alongside criticism of businesses wasting money on AI initiatives and of the longer-term economics of money-losing AI labs.

As global AI stocks spiralled down, Indian IT stocks — priced for disruption — began to soar on their 'anti-AI' advantage.

Results gave the trade a fundamental anchor

HCLTech's strong profit growth, higher AI revenue and improved growth guidance lifted sentiment across the sector, said Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management at Motilal Oswal Financial Services. HCLTech reported 21% year-on-year growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 5,132 crore for the second quarter of FY27. The results land alongside Infosys CEO Salil Parekh's statement that AI services could be nearly half of Infosys's work in two to three years — evidence, for bulls, that AI is a revenue line for Indian IT rather than only a threat to it.

What analysts say comes next

Axis Securities remains cautiously optimistic about the sector. The pace of global AI adoption over the next two to three years remains the key concern for earnings growth and valuations, said Krishna Sanghavi, CIO Equity at Mahindra Manulife Mutual Fund — but if questions over AI's commercial viability slow its rollout, market concerns over Indian IT could ease. Gaurav Garg, head of research at Lemonn Market desk, said the sector may stay positive in the near term on improving sentiment and buying interest after HCLTech's results, though some profit-booking and volatility cannot be ruled out after a rally this sharp.

Views cited are those of the respective brokerages and analysts as reported by The Economic Times; they are not investment advice.
